raw_segments.text: He comes in last. I am not looking at the arch, yet I see him enter.
I try to concentrate my attention on those netting needles, on the meshes of the purse
I am forming. I wish to think only of the work I have in my hands, to see only the silver
beads and silk threads that lie in my lap. Whereas, I distinctly behold his figure, and
I inevitably recall the moment when I last saw it.
Just after I had rendered him, what he deemed an essential service, and he holding my hand
and looking down on my face, surveyed me with eyes that revealed a heart full and eager to
overflow, in whose emotions I had apart. How near had I approached him at that moment?
What had occurred since, calculated to change his and my relative positions? Yet now, how distant,
how far estranged we were, so far estranged, that I did not expect him to come and speak to me.
I did not wonder, when, without looking at me,
he took a seat at the other side of the room and began conversing with some of the ladies.
